svg.title: The local vector incidence inverse pair
svg.desc: A point-output kernel with constant input misses the matched nonzero diagonal conormal but still acts nontrivially on holomorphic coefficients. The actual source comparison retains a whole common polynomial connection factor. Reduced derivative torsion then gives two constant time directions and an output with zero time covector. Both globalizers contribute a total of N plus one derivatives. The two coefficient products have the same nonzero scalar, so one reverse normalization gives both inverses. The strict cutoff module-action comparison remains separate.
svg.text: The local vector incidence inverse pair
Whole connection factor · exact source roofs · one nonzero scalar normalization
1. Vanishing only on the matched graph is insufficient
C = C{t=0} ⊠ CY , Y = projective line
ΦC OY = C{0} ⊗ RΓ(Y,OY) ≠ 0
u = t, w = t′ − t: kernel covector (α,0), diagonal covector (0,−τ).
The kernel retains nonzero output covectors over zero input covectors.
Derivative torsion alone does not make its coefficient output vanish.
Actual point-output obstruction: VIT.1–VIT.2, VIT.25.
2. Retain the whole common polynomial connection
F(M) = C[u] ⊗ M, Du = ∂u
The mapping column [C[u] → C[u]] uses −∂u.
h(f) = −∫0u f(v) dv, dh + hd = 1 − iε
τ-torsion in the reduced algebra gives Cu ⊠ Cw ⊠ Sol(K).
Both endpoint times are constant; the output has τt = 0.
Whole complexes, reduced roofs and coefficient descent: VIT.3–VIT.18.
3. Both globalizers contribute N + 1 derivatives
hN,1 = DtN+1 h ; h′1,N = DsN+1 h′
The actual inverse derivative denominators cancel these exact powers.
a F(b) = λX εX , b G(a) = λY εY
Coherence and a ≠ 0 give λX = λY = λ ≠ 0.
b̃ = λ−1 b
a F(b̃) = εX , b̃ G(a) = εY
These are actual local vector-derived coefficient inverses.
The compatible strict cutoff module action remains a separate condition.
Ordered density, scalar comparison and actual inverses: VIT.19–VIT.30.
